title: Power-Up Buffer for High-Risk Days
dataSources: Life score (`lifeos:score`), quests / tasks (`quest:task`), habit streaks (`streak:status`), life achievements (`achievement:life`), household leaderboard (`household:leaderboard`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The parody-the-enterprise meta layer — a Personal NOC (house-health wall), Personal SOC (entry / impossible-travel), Personal SRE (SLOs on your own habits), and a gamification layer (XP, achievements, streaks, household leaderboards) — all computed in Splunk over `index=personal`.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lifeos:score risk_level=high
| stats avg(buffer_points) as avg_buffer, count as risky_days by domain
| sort avg_buffer
description: Shows whether high-risk days have enough buffer points, prep, or margin attached before they hit.
value: Hard days go better when extra slack exists in the system; this query checks whether that slack is real.
implementation: Track risk level and buffer points on daily `lifeos:score` events and average them by domain.
visualization: Table of high-risk domains with average buffer points.
grandmaExplanation: It counts whether the tough days in life have enough extra margin built around them.
